etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From the 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 増(ま)す (masu).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese, as the long form of 我 (wa) below.
Compound of 我 (wa, see below) + れ (-re, nominalizing suffix).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese 膨る (pukuru), following 下二段活用 (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”), from Proto-Japonic *pukoru.
Development
Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru.
Compare 膨らむ (fukuramu, “to swell, to get bigger”), 膨らます (fukuramasu, “to make swell, to fill up”), and 袋 (fukuro, “bag”), from the way a bag is filled with items.
First cited to the Man’yōshū, completed sometime after 759 CE.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Shift from verb 重(おも)んずる (omonzuru), by natural progression from サ行変格活用 (sa-gyō henkaku katsuyō, “s-irregular conjugation”) verbs ending in -uru to 上一段活用 (kami ichidan katsuyō, “upper monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -iru.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese.
From stem kasu-, cognate with its active counterpart 霞(かす)める (kasumeru, “to blur, to obscure”), adjective かすか (kasuka, “faint, dim”, and its classical form 幽(かすけ)し (kasukeshi)), adverb かすかす (kasukasu, “barely”), verb 掠(かす)める (kasumeru, “to rob; to sweep over”),, and verbs 擦(かす)る (kasuru, “to graze, to touch lightly”) and かすれる (kasureru, “to graze; to be blurred; to be hoarse”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Cognate with 霞(かす)む (kasumu, “to grow hazy, to become blurry”) above.
